_comment: Every colour the asset map draws in. Single source of truth: AssetMap.astro imports this and scripts/test-contrast.mjs checks each entry against the sampled ocean colours of every basemap in basemap-ocean.json. Add a colour here, not in the component.
_bars: What a particle ramp has to clear, in CIEDE2000. Here rather than in a script because the map now applies these at runtime and scripts/test-contrast.mjs proves the result against the same numbers — two copies would let the gate check a bar the map does not enforce. `background` is the one a particle cannot fail: it is a thin moving line with nothing behind it but the water. `marker` is far lower on purpose, because a still outlined dot is separated by shape long before hue. `apart` holds the two velocity fields away from each other, at the background bar, since drifting lines have nothing but colour to tell them apart.
_currents: The starting ramp, and the fallback. The map picks its particle colours at runtime now (see contrast.ts), so this is what is drawn before the first resolve and whenever the background cannot be identified — an unknown basemap, say. It is still gated as a fixed ramp against every water tone, because that is exactly the case it still serves. The current particle ramp — vivid coral, #ff8e73 to #ffa083, slow to fast. Redder and considerably more saturated than the pale coral it replaced, which read as washed out over deep water. It was pale amber before that, and changed because of where it failed: GEBCO paints shallow banks a pale mint, and the amber sat ΔE 21.8 from that tone — under the bar, and invisible on exactly the water this map is most used to look at. It passed the gate anyway, because coverage was weighted by prevalence and the shelf is only 4.9% of ocean pixels; the abyssal plain outvoted it. Saturating toward red costs marker separation and buys background separation, which is the right way round for a velocity field: the worst water tone goes 24.2 to 30.1 while the storm red goes 24.0 to 20.9 and the saildrone orange 24.4 to 19.2. Both markers stay well above the marker bar, and both are filled, outlined, stationary dots that shape separates from a drifting trail. It stops short of the most saturated red available. At full chroma the ramp reaches ΔE 17.1 of the storm markers — still passing, but the storms are the one feature the hurricane page exists for, and a vivid red field around a vivid red dot is a poor trade for a shade more vividness.
_wind: The wind particle ramp — deep forest green, #003b00 to #004900, slow to fast, and dark where the currents' coral is pale. Two things decide a velocity field's colour and they are not the markers: it has to clear the **background**, which is the bathymetry in all its tones and whichever colour scale has replaced it, and it has to contrast with the **other** velocity field, since the two share the screen and a drifting line has no shape to be told apart by. This clears every water tone of both basemaps at worst 38.1, every marker-safe colormap at 24.6, and sits ΔE 69.0 from the coral — the largest separation available from it. It replaced a lemon yellow, which was chosen while coverage was still weighted by area and the pale shelf could be outvoted: measured tone by tone, that yellow sat 20.8 from GEBCO's mint shelf and 17.9 from the haline scale, and carried four background concessions. This carries none. No yellow can fix that — searched, and the ones that clear the shelf fail the colour scales instead, because the two constraints pull opposite ways. Its closest approach to anything is ΔE 19.8, to the Argo dots' dark outline — a hairline round a gold fill this clears by 50, and a marker is a still, filled, outlined dot that shape separates from a moving trail long before hue does.
_colormaps: Colour scales the reader can choose, in two groups, and the split is measured rather than editorial. Whichever map is on becomes the water beneath every marker and particle, so scripts/test-contrast.mjs measures every stop of every map against every feature colour by CIEDE2000. The five in markerSafe clear 22 everywhere along their length; nothing else does, and that is not a flaw in the others — a full-gamut colormap sweeps through the whole wheel, so somewhere along it it passes close to a marker. Measured worst clearance: cmo.haline 11.2, hsv 7.5, jet 6.4, viridis 6.2, grey 5.5, turbo 4.2, inferno 3.0. The five safe ones exist because they were built to dodge the feature gamut, which is exactly why they look less like the standard maps. The standard set is offered anyway — it is the reader's map and these are the scales oceanography actually speaks — but the picker groups them apart and the defaults stay in the safe set. The markers keep their dark outlines, which is what carries them on a background the fill contrast does not. The cmo.* and matplotlib entries are ten-stop samples of the published maps, close enough to be recognisable, not the exact tables.
_defaultColormap: Which map each field starts on. A reader can change it; this is the opening choice, and both are the scales oceanography actually reads these fields with — jet for temperature, cmo.haline for salinity. Neither is in markerSafe: measured, jet's worst clearance from a marker is 6.4 and cmo.haline's is 11.2, against the bar of 22. So a platform sitting on the wrong stop of the opening view has less separation than the gate demands everywhere else. That is a deliberate trade of familiarity against separation — the markers keep their dark outlines, which is what carries them on a background the fill contrast does not, and the five markerSafe scales stay one click away in the picker. Ice concentration opens on cmo.ice for the same reason: it is the scale sea ice is read with, near-black through blue to white, and white at the top is what makes a full pack look like one. Its worst clearance from a marker is 6.6, so it is exempt alongside the other two — and the exemption costs less here than it looks, because the layer only paints above 15% concentration, which is a tenth of the ocean and not where the gliders are.
_defaultExempt: Fields whose default colormap is knowingly not marker-safe. Named here rather than reclassified, so scripts/test-contrast.mjs reports the cost on every run instead of it disappearing. Drop a field from this list and the gate fails until its default is a safe map again.
_measure: The measuring line. Dark rather than bright because it is drawn over everything and must not be mistaken for a platform or a current; charcoal was the only candidate clearing both bathymetries while staying clear of every feature colour. It carries a light halo, which like the track casings is an outline rather than a feature colour and so is themed in CSS rather than gated here.
_concessions: Every place a colour on this map knowingly sits under the ΔE 22 bar, with the measured distance and the reason. Recorded here rather than by lowering the threshold, which would quietly cover every future clash as well. scripts/test-contrast.mjs reports each on every run and checks the list **both ways**: a pair under the bar with no concession fails, and a concession for a pair that actually clears fails too. Without the second half the list rots — a clash that got fixed would still be listed, and the listing would stop meaning anything. Same bargain markerSafe strikes with the colormaps. What makes these tolerable is that a particle is a thin moving trail and the things it is close to are either filled dots with dark outlines or a whole-field raster: form and motion separate them where colour does not. That argument has limits, and the honest place to see them is this list getting longer.
